gaps.quote: Undoing the exchange moves each output back to its input role
gaps.note: The page never defines an operation that undoes the exchange of roles or says which frames it uses. The reader cannot check that applying it returns each output to its input role with the correct operator, so the conclusion that the undoing needs no sign or frame correction is not followable.

gaps.term: scratch role has rho(w) = w with sign +1
gaps.quote: For a scratch role the construction has $\rho(w)=w$ with sign $+1$ (cited)
gaps.note: This is a property of how the construction treats scratch roles, which is the page's own concept. The page gives only a citation and does not say why the scratch-role wiring fixes each scratch role and carries sign +1, so the reader cannot check it.

gaps.term: every role keeps the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: This is the claim that the network applies the endpoint operator at every role, which is what the page's account of computing a result depends on. It is supported only by a citation; the page does not say what the cited result states about the network's wiring or why it applies to this network.
